brief.outcome: Get the median GitHub Actions pipeline from about 40 minutes to under 15 minutes, and cut random failures (runs that fail and then pass on retry) from roughly 1 in 6 to fewer than 1 in 50, within six weeks, without dropping test coverage or any required check.

ambition.goal_beyond: The team trusts a green build and merges quickly, because a red build means a real problem and CI stops draining time and money.
rungs: Speed up the pipeline and fix the most obvious flaky tests
Find from the run history exactly where the 40 minutes and the random failures come from, and fix the causes in order of payback, without weakening a check
Keep it true without being asked: a time budget and a flaky budget that flag drift before the team feels it again
ambition.judge: GitHub Actions run history itself (durations, run attempts and conclusions pulled from the API for the same window before and after), plus the required-checks list and the coverage report compared before and after

brief.deliverable: Reviewed pull requests that speed up the workflows and fix or fence the flaky tests, landed one at a time by the team, with a before and after readout against the run history.
done: Run history pulled and checked: durations, retries and queue time
Required checks and coverage recorded before any change, as the baseline to prove nothing was dropped
Every cause hypothesis marked supported, refuted or unknown with numbers
Platform lead chose the changes, with reasons recorded
Draft pull requests ready, each showing its measured gain and its check list
Changes landed by the team one at a time and read back
Median under 15 minutes and random failures under 1 in 50 over a full window, or an honest miss with the numbers
Budget rules proposed for the platform lead to accept or reject
guardrails: Test coverage does not drop below its recorded baseline
Every required check stays required and still runs the same tests (no check removed, weakened or made optional)
Random failure rate ends under 1 in 50 runs
CI bill stays at or below the reported 2,800 dollars a month
Pull requests are reviewed before any change merges
limits: Changes go in only through reviewed pull requests
GitHub access is read plus draft pull requests; the team merges
Coverage and required checks are not to be traded for speed
assets: GitHub Actions run history and workflow files
Monorepo with a Python backend and a TypeScript front end
brief.data_home: A folder of files in this project (the owner did not choose, so we chose)
brief.technical_level: Not stated by the owner. Hand changes over as draft pull requests with plain notes for the platform lead.
unknowns: Which jobs, steps and tests take the time, and how much is queue time
Which tests or jobs cause the random failures, and whether retries are automatic or manual
Runner types and sizes, and whether any runners are self-hosted
Whether dependencies and build outputs are cached today
Current test coverage figure and the list of required checks
Whether the GitHub MCP exposes job logs and the billing usage report, or the owner must export them

answers.question: What is the stack?
answers.answer: Monorepo with a Python backend and TypeScript front end, GitHub Actions

answers.question: How bad is it, and how do you know?
answers.answer: Median pipeline about 40 minutes; roughly 1 in 6 runs fails and passes on retry (GitHub Actions history, reported)

answers.question: What does it cost?
answers.answer: CI bill about 2,800 dollars a month

answers.question: What access do we have?
answers.answer: GitHub MCP with read access and draft pull requests

answers.question: What counts as fixed, by when?
answers.answer: Median under 15 minutes and fewer than 1 in 50 random failures within six weeks, without dropping test coverage or required checks

answers.question: How do changes go in, and who decides?
answers.answer: Through reviewed pull requests; the platform lead decides

research.approach: Practitioners treat CI speed and flakiness as measurement problems first. They pull the run history, work out the critical path (the chain of jobs that sets the wall-clock time) and the waste around it: repeated installs, no cache, everything running on every change, runs for commits already superseded, and queue time. For flakiness they find runs that failed and then passed on the same commit, group them by failure signature, and fix causes (shared state, time, sleeps, remote services) or fence a test in a time-limited quarantine, never by deleting checks. Each change is landed alone so its effect is measurable, and the pipeline's required checks and coverage are recorded first so nothing is silently dropped.

sources.title: Dependency caching reference (GitHub Docs)
sources.note: Cache keys built from lock-file hashes, restore-keys order, 10 GB per repository default with least-recently-used eviction, caches unused for 7 days removed, branch scoping. Page shows no date; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs (GitHub Docs)
sources.note: cancel-in-progress cancels a superseded run; group names must include the workflow or one workflow can cancel another; unsuitable for deployments that must finish. Page shows no date; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: GitHub Actions runner pricing (GitHub Docs)
sources.note: Per-minute rates by runner type, so billed minutes by runner can be reconciled with the monthly bill. Standard Linux 2-core x64 listed at 0.006 dollars a minute in the search snippet; confirm on the live page. Accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Flaky tests (pytest documentation)
sources.note: Flakiness comes from uncontrolled state and order dependence; random-order plugins expose it; reruns and non-strict xfail hide it and are risky to leave in permanently. Page shows no date; accessed 2026-11-03.

steps.name: Pull the raw run history with job and step timings, run attempts and queue time
steps.why: The 40 minutes and 1 in 6 are reported; per-job timings and attempt numbers show where time and retries really are.

steps.name: Record required checks, coverage and the bill split before any change
steps.why: A speed gain that quietly drops a check or coverage is a failure; the baseline is the proof.

steps.name: Check the history is complete and the retries are identified
steps.why: Re-runs, cancelled runs and multiple attempts distort medians and the flake rate if not separated.

steps.name: Find the critical path and the waste around it
steps.why: Only changes on the critical path shorten the wall-clock time; caching, selective runs, sharding and cancelling superseded runs each cut a different part.

steps.name: Group retry-then-pass runs by failure signature and cause
steps.why: Flakiness usually concentrates in a few tests or in the environment; causes differ and so do fixes.

steps.name: Rank the changes by minutes saved and failures removed, and let the platform lead choose
steps.why: Changes differ in payback and in risk to the required checks.

steps.name: Make each change as a small pull request with its own measured effect
steps.why: One change per pull request lets the gain be attributed and reverted alone.

steps.name: Land changes one at a time through review and read each back
steps.why: Landing one by one isolates which change moved the numbers.

steps.name: Compare a full window before and after on the same definitions
steps.why: Medians need enough runs and the same counting rules; the flake rate needs a full week or more.

steps.name: Propose a time budget and a flaky budget

pitfalls.text: Speeding up by dropping tests or making checks optional, which breaks the owner's coverage and required-check limit.
Cache keys that never change or change every run, or a cache that is evicted by the 10 GB limit and 7-day rule, so the cache never helps.
Cancel-in-progress with a group name shared across workflows, so one workflow cancels another, or applied to runs that must finish.
Fixing flaky tests by adding retries or longer sleeps, which hides the cause and adds minutes.
Leaving tests in quarantine with no owner or time limit until they stop testing anything.
Judging the gain on a few runs, or comparing windows with different pull request volume.

plan.name: Make CI fast and trustworthy without weakening any check

capabilities.name: Read workflows, runs, jobs and code (GitHub MCP)
capabilities.why: Read workflow files, run history, job timings and test code.

capabilities.name: Draft pull requests (GitHub MCP)
capabilities.why: Open draft pull requests with the changes; nothing is merged by us.

capabilities.name: Export the Actions usage report (owner, GitHub billing)
capabilities.why: Billed minutes by workflow and runner type, if the MCP does not expose them.

capabilities.name: Merge a pull request (platform lead)
capabilities.why: The team merges each reviewed pull request; we do not.

data.name: Actions run history
data.why: The raw material: duration, attempts, conclusion, trigger and queue time for every run.

routes.how: GitHub MCP: list workflow runs for the last 60 days, including attempts.
gh run list --json or the Actions API export, if the MCP limits pages.

data.alternative: If only 100 recent runs can be read, medians are marked low confidence.

data.name: Job and step timings
data.why: Shows the critical path and where time goes inside a job.

routes.how: GitHub MCP: list jobs for a run, with steps.

data.name: Failed job logs and test reports

routes.how: GitHub MCP: job logs for failed attempts; test report artifacts.
Ask the platform lead for the log export if the MCP cannot read logs.

data.alternative: Without logs, flaky runs are ranked by job only and causes stay unknown.

data.name: Actions usage and bill
data.why: Reconcile billed minutes by runner type with the reported 2,800 dollars a month.

routes.how: Platform lead exports the usage report from GitHub billing.

data.alternative: Without it the cost guardrail is checked from run minutes only, marked limited.

data.name: Required checks and coverage baseline
data.why: Proof that no check or coverage was dropped.

routes.how: GitHub MCP: branch protection and the latest coverage artifact.
Ask for the coverage figure if it is not an artifact.

stages.name: Pin down the problem
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Pull the run history
stages.goal: Pull 60 days of workflow runs, job and step timings, run attempts, queue time and failed-attempt logs into one folder.

checks.name: At least 30 days and 500 runs are covered, or the shortfall is stated and medians are marked low confidence
Recomputed median duration of completed pipelines is within 3 minutes of the reported 40, or the difference is explained
Every run records its attempt number and whether a later attempt on the same commit passed

stages.name: Check the data and record what must not change
stages.goal: Check the history is complete and the retry count is right, reconcile minutes with the bill, and record the required checks and coverage as the baseline the changes are held to.

checks.name: Billed minutes from the usage report match minutes summed from jobs within 10%, or the gap is explained (runner multipliers, free minutes)
Cancelled and skipped runs are excluded from medians and counted separately
Every required check name and the latest coverage figure are recorded with a date
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the diagnosis

stages.name: Find where the time and the failures come from
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses: critical path, waste around it, queue time, and the cause of each group of retry-then-pass failures. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every listed hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN with the number behind it
The critical path is drawn from job start and end times, and the minutes on it add up to within 10% of the median
Retry-then-pass runs are grouped by failure signature and the top groups cover at least 70% of them, or the rest is stated
Each main finding names a competing explanation

stages.name: Rank the changes
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked change cards: minutes saved, failures removed, effort, risk to the required checks and how each will be measured.

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card states expected minutes saved on the median and failures removed, and the cards together are checked against the 15-minute target
Every card says which required checks and coverage it touches (none, or named) and how that will be proven unchanged

stages.name: Platform lead chooses
stages.goal: The platform lead picks the cards. Ask for the reason when a top card is passed over. Any card that moves a test out of a required check (quarantine) needs an explicit yes with an owner and a time limit.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are recorded, with the reason wherever the top card was passed over
Any quarantined test has a named owner and a fix-by date no more than 7 days out, or it is not quarantined

stages.name: Draft the pull requests
stages.goal: For each chosen card make one small pull request: caching, selective or parallel jobs, cancelling superseded runs, runner sizing, and fixes for flaky tests at the cause. Each carries its measured effect and its required-check list.

checks.name: Each pull request makes one kind of change and says which card it carries out
Required check names and the tests each runs are identical before and after, shown by a diff of the workflow and branch rules
Each change was run at least 5 times on its branch and the durations are shown, or it is marked NOT TRIALED
Each flaky-test fix passes 50 consecutive runs in CI, or is marked NOT PROVEN
A second reviewer finds no unresolved blocker in any pull request

stages.name: Land the changes one at a time
stages.goal: The platform lead merges the reviewed pull requests one at a time, in the order that isolates each effect, and we read back each result before the next.

checks.name: Each merge has the platform lead's approval recorded first
After each merge, the next 10 runs are read and their median and failure count are recorded
A change that raises median duration or breaks a required check is reverted, not left in

stages.name: Read the results honestly
stages.goal: Compare a full window after the changes with the same-length window before, on the same definitions, and check every guardrail.

checks.name: Both windows have at least 14 days and 200 runs, and pull request volume is within 30% between them, or the difference is stated
Median and random-failure rate use the same definitions as the baseline (attempt rules, exclusions)
Coverage is not below baseline, required checks are identical, and the bill is not above 2,800 dollars a month
A missed target is reported with the numbers and which cards fell short

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Record what worked, propose a time budget and a flaky budget with alert thresholds, and plan the next round.

checks.name: Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this repository, this business or the playbook, and who owns it
The proposed budgets give numeric thresholds (median minutes, retry-then-pass rate) and nothing is switched on without the platform lead's yes

hypotheses.statement: Dependencies and build outputs are reinstalled or rebuilt on every run.
hypotheses.test: Step timings for install and build, and cache hit or miss lines in logs.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Install plus build steps are 25% or more of median pipeline time and cache misses are over 30% of runs.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cache hits are over 90% and these steps are under 10% of the time.

hypotheses.statement: Independent jobs run one after another, so the critical path is long.
hypotheses.test: Job start and end times and needs: dependencies.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The longest chain is 70% or more of wall-clock time and contains jobs with no real dependency.
hypotheses.refute_if: The long chain is a single slow job.

hypotheses.statement: A small share of tests dominates test time.
hypotheses.test: Per-test or per-file durations from test reports.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The slowest 10% of tests are 50% or more of test time.

hypotheses.statement: The monorepo runs backend and front end jobs on every change.
hypotheses.test: Files changed per pull request against jobs that ran.
hypotheses.confirm_if: 40% or more of pull request runs touch only one side but run both.
hypotheses.refute_if: Path filtering already limits runs and under 15% of runs are unnecessary.

hypotheses.statement: Runs for commits already replaced by a newer push on the same pull request waste minutes.
hypotheses.test: Runs on the same pull request that were still going or finished after a newer push.
hypotheses.confirm_if: 15% or more of billed minutes are on superseded runs.

hypotheses.statement: Time is lost waiting for a runner.
hypotheses.test: Queue time (created to started) per job.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Median queue time is 10% or more of wall-clock time.
hypotheses.refute_if: Queue time is under 2 minutes at the 95th percentile.

hypotheses.statement: A few tests or jobs cause most random failures.
hypotheses.test: Group retry-then-pass runs by failing test or step and error text.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The top 5 signatures cover 60% or more of retry-then-pass runs.
hypotheses.refute_if: No signature is above 10% of them.

hypotheses.statement: Random failures come from the environment (network, service startup, runner limits), not test logic.
hypotheses.test: Error text for timeouts, connection refused, out-of-memory, rate limits.
hypotheses.confirm_if: 30% or more of retry-then-pass runs match environment signatures.

hypotheses.statement: Tests fail because they share state or depend on order or time.
hypotheses.test: Re-run the failing tests alone, in random order and in parallel.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The failures reproduce in random order or parallel and not alone.
hypotheses.refute_if: They fail the same way alone or never reproduce.

measurement.window: At least 14 days after the last change lands, against the 14 days before the first change, with pull request volume within 30%.
measurement.min_volume: At least 200 completed pipeline runs in each window; below that, the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.
measurement.stop_rule: Revert a change at once if median duration rises, a required check is missing, or coverage falls below baseline; otherwise read the full window before a verdict.
